priorAtomicRecord.reason: Two independent goal-core reviews agree. A: The air/vacuum comparison and explanation through air resistance form one causal comparison in both languages. Equal vacuum velocities presuppose matched initial conditions; the feather/ball example does not establish a universal rule that lighter objects fall more slowly in air. B: Changing the medium tests one explanation for the different falls. With matched releases in the same gravitational field, the bodies have equal velocities at equal times in vacuum. In air, drag relative to the body’s weight matters, so mass alone cannot determine the ordering. Evidence: curricula/DE/Gymnasium/quality/goal-evidence/2026-11-24/e1-current-nine-v1/core-independent-review/dual-summary.actual.json

currentAtomicRecord.reviewer: Codex non-author integrator of actual blind gpt-6.1-sol/ultra and gpt-6.2-astra/ultra exact-current FALL reviews
currentAtomicRecord.reason: Both fresh exact-current reviews confirm semantic atomicity after the matching-initial-conditions clarification. A: Der aktuelle bilinguale Text verlangt einen kohärenten Vergleich desselben Fallvorgangs unter gleichen Anfangsbedingungen mit und ohne Luft. Die Beobachtungen werden durch eine gemeinsame physikalische Beziehung organisiert: gleicher Fall ohne Luftwiderstand und unterschiedlich bedeutsamer Widerstand in Luft. Beide Medien sind Vergleichsbedingungen dieser einen Kompetenz. Eine zusätzliche Bestimmung von g, quantitative Widerstandsgesetze oder allgemeine Modellbewertung werden nicht verlangt. B: Holding the release conditions fixed gives the two observations a common physical explanation. The bodies share gravitational acceleration in a vacuum. In air, drag can affect their accelerations differently. Predicting how the comparison changes when air is removed demonstrates the whole relationship in one task. Evidence: curricula/DE/Gymnasium/quality/goal-description-review/physik/rollout-v1/2026-11-24/e1-current-eight-v2/actual-execution/
